acceptance_evidence: A public CLI initializes and runs an optimization campaign through baseline, evaluation, improvement, retest, promotion or rejection, and a terminal stopping rule.
Deterministic fake providers prove multiple rounds, non-regression promotion, no-progress stopping, budget stopping, interruption resume, and artifact tamper detection without model calls.
The live Claude command uses a fresh nonpersistent streamed session with pinned prompt/plugin/settings inputs and captures transcript, hook, timing, token, and exit metadata.
The evaluator combines hard gates with frozen weighted dimensions and rejects any hard-gate failure or substantive-dimension regression even when the total score improves.
The improver receives only the incumbent, failed dimensions, bounded transcript evidence, and development evidence; it cannot read holdout results or mutate global configuration.
Focused and full repository tests pass, and documentation includes a zero-cost dry run plus the separately authorized live workflow.
assumptions: The first implementation can use injected fake runner, evaluator, and improver components to prove orchestration while leaving paid execution operator-triggered.
The established rubric will be represented as a versioned JSON document and can be refined without changing the loop state machine.
A fixed audited hook executable will consume declarative candidate policy; arbitrary hook source generation is excluded.
Codex will be the default independent evaluator and improvement provider for live campaigns, but the core loop will depend on interfaces rather than a specific harness.

constraints: Do not execute a paid Claude or Codex campaign during local implementation verification.
Do not modify the user's global Claude configuration or promote a candidate globally.
Candidate generation may change prompt text and declarative hook policy, but must not execute model-generated hook code.
Every round, result, evaluation, candidate, and promotion decision must be immutable or append-only and safely resumable.
Holdout evidence must not be exposed to the improvement step.
Provider failure, timeout, malformed output, budget exhaustion, or integrity mismatch must stop without promoting a candidate.
desired_outcome: Deliver a locally verified, resumable controller that runs fresh Claude harness candidates against pinned scenarios, evaluates them with the established Claude-versus-Codex criteria, generates one bounded improvement at a time, retests, and promotes only a non-regressing candidate within fixed safety and efficiency budgets.

facts.statement: The existing controller already persists immutable manifests and run results, resumes idempotently, enforces run ceilings, and reports fake campaign results.
The existing live path validates isolation and then deliberately refuses provider execution.
Claude Code supports noninteractive streamed JSON, session-local prompt and settings overrides, hook-event output, fresh no-persistence sessions, and session-only plugin loading in the installed CLI.

The accepted predecessor plan requires a frozen comparison rubric, hard evidence gates, champion-challenger promotion, bounded prompt/hook-policy candidates, and no global mutation during experiments.

rationale: The repository already contains an immutable campaign controller, task fixtures, provider argv builders, isolation qualification, and fake-run tests. The requested loop extends those existing seams with candidate, grading, improvement, and promotion state plus a live subprocess boundary, so implementation and local verification are required.

assumptions: Fake components are sufficient to establish local controller correctness; live behavioral superiority remains a later measurement.
recommendation.choice: Extend the existing experiment controller with an injected champion-challenger optimization state machine and qualified live boundaries.
recommendation.rationale: This reuses proven immutable storage and scheduling, makes the full loop testable without quota, and separates orchestration correctness from later provider and global-promotion authorization.
tradeoffs: The initial implementation will not automatically install the winning harness globally.
A frozen rubric and declarative hook policy add configuration that must be versioned carefully.
